canvas-01.description: The central village of Old Bridge, on the west bank of the South River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch on the index sheet of the atlas. The map is bounded by Brunswick Turnpike on the west and South River Road on the east, with the river itself drawn along the right edge. Main Street, printed as Main (Locust), crosses the sheet near the bottom, with the Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division and its depot, freight platform and siding just south of it. North of Main, Pine, Willow, Maple and Chestnut run diagonally between the turnpike and South River Road, crossed by Church and Oak, forming small blocks of frame dwellings with outbuildings, coops and auto sheds. Institutions include the public school between Pine and Willow, the Baptist Church, the Town Hall and the Simpson M.E. Church on Willow, and St. Thomas R.C. Church in the open ground at the top. Along Main are stores, a post office, a pool room, the Old Bridge Hotel and the Old Bridge Garage at the turnpike corner, and at the east end the former Chas. Layton grist mill, not in operation. South of the railroad, Brunswick Turnpike runs beside a loop of the South River past the fire house and fire bell tower to meet Matawan Road and Squire, where Squires Garage stands. The upper left of the sheet carries the index of specials, the key, a key map of the village at 800 feet to an inch and a location map of New Jersey; these are outside the mask. A note on the fire department is printed inside the river loop. North on this sheet points to the upper right.
notes: Brunswick Turnpike north of Main is today Old Bridge Turnpike; south of Main its line is followed by Matawan Road.
Willow is today Kossman Street; Church is Rutgers Road; South River Road is River Road.
Matawan Road between Main and Squire is today Emerson Street.
Main is also labelled Locust on the sheet.
The Kossman Street / River Road junction was rejected (about 8 m from the fit); the modern street end appears realigned.

Printed sheet 1: index, legend, key map at 800 ft (masked out), state location inset (masked out), and the main map at 100 ft: Main (Locust), Brunswick Turnpike, Pine, Chestnut, Willow, Maple, Church, Oak, South River Rd, Squire, Matawan Rd. One part (config canvas-01). Drawn with north about 32 degrees clockwise of up; the north arrow shows about 14 degrees.

sheet-2-1.description: The southern part of Old Bridge across the South River from the village centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points almost to the right of the sheet. At the top right the Iron Bridge carries the road over the South River to Matawan Road on the far bank. From the bridge a road runs diagonally to a five-way junction with Englishtown Road, then continues south-west as Greystone. Matawan branches south from it past Carney to Charles, which loops back to Greystone. On the west are Leonard and Brunswick Gardens Road with long narrow lots, and Jasmine Terrace, marked not graded. The area is thinly built: frame dwellings, many coops, sheds and auto houses, a few stores along Matawan near Carney, and Park Dills Saw Mill, not in operation, near Greystone and a street marked not named. Marsh borders the river along the east side. Large tracts in the lower left and centre are left blank. Today State Route 18 crosses this area diagonally and most of the drawn streets are gone or realigned; only the Matawan and Carney corner and the bridge road remain identifiable.
notes: Matawan and the diagonal road to the Iron Bridge are today Old Matawan Road; Carney is Kearney Avenue.
Placed from two points only (Kearney Avenue / Old Matawan Road detected, and Matawan Road / Old Matawan Road hand-picked at the east end of the Iron Bridge); helmert, low confidence.
A block corner at Charles and Matawan lies about 10 m from the nearest modern parcel corner.
An 'RD' label is printed on the diagonal road between the Iron Bridge and the Englishtown Road junction; 'Greystone' is printed on its continuation to the south-west.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (main, right and bottom) Leonard, Brunswick Gardens Rd, Jasmine Ter., Greystone, Englishtown Rd, Matawan, Carney, Charles, the Iron Bridge over the South River, drawn with north about 83 degrees clockwise of up; part 2 (inset top left, heavy line) Charles, John, William at Jamesburg Turnpike and the P.R.R. Amboy Division, north about 35 degrees. Much of part 1 is crossed by today's State Route 18; only two junctions survive.

sheet-2-2.description: An inset in the upper left of sheet 2, set off by a heavy line, showing a small block of streets north of the railroad and east of the village centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. William runs up the sheet from Jamesburg Turnpike, crossed by John and Charles, which run west to the edge of the sheet marked no exposure. The Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division runs along the south side of Jamesburg Turnpike with several parallel tracks and a spur curving north-east toward the brick works on sheet 3; the dash-dot match line A-B on the right joins this inset to the top part of sheet 3. The blocks hold scattered frame dwellings with coops, sheds and auto houses, a store at William and Jamesburg Turnpike, and a ruin of a fire on Charles. The ground east of William is mostly open.
notes: Jamesburg Turnpike is today Bordentown Avenue.
Placed from three junctions along William Street only (helmert); rotation rests on that one street.

100 ft. sheet-3-1.description: The works of The Old Bridge Enameled Brick & Tile Co., manufacturers of wall and floor tile, on the north side of Jamesburg Turnpike east of the village, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The plant is a dense group of frame and brick buildings: a long kiln shed with rows of round kilns, sagger houses, color and drying rooms, wash house, washing and grinding, pressing rooms, sorting and packing, ceramic departments, a bisque and dipping department, a ware house, a machine shop and an engine house with boilers, a water tank and a concrete clay storage with raised runways. A clay trestle and a coal trestle curve across the top of the sheet from the railroad spur. Below the turnpike the Pennsylvania Railroad Amboy Division runs with several tracks, and two small buildings stand south of it. A printed note gives the watchman, heating, power and water supply arrangements. The dash-dot match line A-B on the left joins this part to the inset on sheet 2.
notes: Jamesburg Turnpike is today Bordentown Avenue.

No street junction: anchored on one point carried from sheet 2 part 2 (the match line at the north edge of the turnpike) with the sheet scale and a rotation set to the modern bearing of Bordentown Avenue; low confidence.

50 ft. Two parts: part 1 (top) Old Bridge Enameled Brick & Tile Co. on the north side of Jamesburg Turnpike (Bordentown Avenue) with the P.R.R. Amboy Division, continuing sheet 2 part 2 across match line A-B; part 2 (bottom) Brookfield Glass Co., insulators, 'Located 1 1/4 miles N.E. of P.O.', rail sidings and the South River, no street.
